clue.text: Fine material in suit dressing Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth

indicators.note: the suit wraps round the royal letters as clothing dresses a body

parts.note: a case at law is a suit
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A monarch is clothed in a suit of some luxurious fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' here is a lawsuit, not clothing; 'dressing' wraps it round the royal letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is a soft, costly goat-wool cloth, a fine fabric.

clue.text: Overweight, married man under a ton

indicators.note: in a down clue the husband sits below the hundred

parts.note: a ton is a hundred, C in Roman numerals
hubby is a husband

explanation.surface: A husband is heavy, though still under a ton.
explanation.definitionFit: Chubby means plump, carrying a little too much weight.

clue.text: Beneath turf, burrow wet

indicators.note: in this down entry the burrow comes below the turf

parts.note: a sod is a piece of turf
a den is an animal's burrow

explanation.surface: Under the grass an animal's burrow lies soaked.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodden means soaked through, thoroughly drenched.

clue.text: Spread betting finally grasped by horse

indicators.note: the female horse holds the letter within her

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

indicators.note: the closing letter of betting

explanation.surface: A spread bet is made on a racehorse.
explanation.definitionFit: Marge is short for margarine, a butter substitute you spread on bread.

clue.text: Might one be slated for too incompetent performance, primarily?

indicators.note: a botched job jumbles these words into a mess
the first letter of performance

explanation.surface: Would a critic pan a show for being far too inept?
explanation.walkthrough: 'incompetent' scrambles FOR TOO into ROOFTO; 'primarily' adds P.
explanation.definitionFit: A house top is often covered in slates, so it may literally be slated.

clue.text: Failure of mathematician, possibly, to find parcels from China

definitions.meaning: a stupid calculation, a ..., is what a poor mathematician might produce
small steamed dumplings served in Cantonese cuisine

explanation.surface: A sum gone wrong somehow leads to a delivery from China.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim sum are bite-sized Chinese dumplings, little wrapped parcels of filling.

clue.text: Waste of animal in dinosaur not half tragic, reptile now extinct

indicators.note: the droppings go inside the jumbled letters
a tragic state is a disastrous one, mixing the letters up
half the letters of dinosaur are dropped

parts.note: guano is the droppings of seabirds or bats

explanation.surface: Animal droppings inside a dinosaur fossil: a sad end for an extinct reptile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' keeps the first half of the word, which 'tragic' rearranges to IDON before the droppings go 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguanodon was a large plant-eating dinosaur, long vanished.

clue.text: Quarter of a pint drunk by squiffy gentlefolk initially connecting romantically

indicators.note: the small measure goes down inside the pair of letters, as a drink goes into drinkers
the first letters of squiffy and gentlefolk

parts.note: a noggin is a small measure, a quarter of a pint

explanation.surface: Tipsy toffs, a little drink inside them, start getting amorous.
explanation.walkthrough: Squiffy is British slang for slightly drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Snogging is British slang for kissing, a romantic clinch.

clue.text: Second: loser upset, ending in theory with sullen disposition

parts.note: mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: the defeated party is overturned, his letters shuffled
the last letter of theory

explanation.surface: A beaten candidate, briefly upset, theorises gloomily.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting morosely is behaving in a gloomy, sullen manner.

clue.text: Feebler party? Don't cook enough goulash for starter

parts.note: to underdo food is to cook it too little

indicators.note: the first course of goulash, so its opening letter

explanation.surface: Advice to a weak host: leave the goulash a bit raw for the first course.
explanation.definitionFit: An underdog is the side expected to lose, the weaker contender.

clue.text: Sense of wit I'm not sure is found in time

indicators.note: the hesitation sits within the period of time

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time
um is the sound of someone unsure

explanation.surface: Someone hesitantly says comic timing is what wit needs.
explanation.definitionFit: A sense of humour is the capacity for wit and seeing the funny side.

clue.text: Sparkle in opening of bubbly and port

indicators.note: the first letter of bubbly

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: There is fizz in a newly opened bottle of champagne and port.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio means vivacity and spirit, a lively sparkle.

clue.text: Feeding bird, fine yeoman

indicators.note: the abbreviation is fed into the middle of the bird's name

parts.note: the bee-eater is a colourful insect-eating bird
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A bird is pecking at food, and a yeoman looks on fine.
explanation.walkthrough: BEEFEATER is the bee-eater with F slipped between its two Es.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefeaters are the Yeoman Warders who guard the Tower of London.

clue.text: Old drink tipped back into tiramisu, generously

indicators.note: the run of letters is poured out backwards, as if tipped
the drink is buried inside the dessert words

explanation.surface: An old tipple is poured generously over tiramisu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' marks SUGEN, sitting across 'tiramisu, generously'; 'tipped back' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Negus was an eighteenth-century hot punch of wine, water, sugar and spice.

clue.text: Lean forward

definitions.meaning: to lean a thing against a wall is to support it so
in rugby a ... is one of the front-row forwards

explanation.definitionFit: Prop as a verb means to rest against something; in rugby it names a forward position.

clue.text: Noble right hooks producing shiner

indicators.note: the word right catches the nobleman and holds him inside

parts.note: an earl is a noble

explanation.surface: A lord lands a right hook and gives someone a black eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shiner' suggests a black eye from the boxing surface, but here it is simply something that shines.
explanation.definitionFit: A rear light is the lamp that glows on the back of a vehicle, so it shines.

clue.text: Shoved in mouth, racket first perhaps?

indicators.note: the noise is pushed inside the word for the mouth

parts.note: oral means of the mouth
din means a racket, loud noise

explanation.surface: Something rammed into a mouth, and a tennis racket first in line?
explanation.definitionFit: First is an example of an ordinal number, one giving position in a sequence.

clue.text: After rewrite of scene, lad missing the filthy bits?

indicators.note: redrafting the words rearranges their letters

explanation.surface: A censor revises a scene, cutting the lad and the smut.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleansed means washed clean, with the dirt removed.

clue.text: To do well, shift about two religious texts

indicators.note: the dress goes around the scriptures

parts.note: a shift is a simple dress, as is a gown

indicators.note: the abbreviation appears twice over

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, is a set of religious texts

explanation.surface: Moving a couple of holy books helps you succeed.
explanation.walkthrough: GOWN opens as G...OWN to hold OTOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to act with great enthusiasm or lavish expense, really splashing out.

clue.text: US writer back to poke fat cat

indicators.note: the reversed writer pokes into the fat, sitting inside it

parts.note: lard is pig fat

indicators.note: the writer's name runs in reverse

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, American author

explanation.surface: An American author returns to prod a plump cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the writer to give EOP, and 'to poke' sets that inside the fat.
explanation.definitionFit: The leopard is a large spotted wild member of the feline family.

clue.text: European from England, an Englishman

indicators.note: the nationality is taken from within these words

explanation.surface: A European from England turns out to be an Englishman.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Denmark is a European by nationality.

clue.text: Day, then week, missing little prayer?

parts.note: Mon is short for Monday

indicators.note: the small word is lacking from the period of seven days

parts.note: wee means small, little

explanation.surface: A day, then a week, without saying even a small prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes WEE from WEEK, leaving only K.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloistered religious brother spends his days praying, so he is one who prays.

clue.text: One entering the game not entirely surprisingly a great success

indicators.note: the numeral comes into the scrambled letters
the letters fall in an unexpected order
the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone joining a game partway through turns out to be a smash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' trims THE GAME to THEGAM, 'surprisingly' scrambles it, and I goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A megahit is a smash, a huge box-office or chart triumph.

clue.text: Hit wicket, for example, unusual

definitions.meaning: in cricket, hit wicket is one way a batter can be dismissed

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is a method of dismissal; as a phrase it means bizarre or extreme.

clue.text: Infant in very old winter vehicle

indicators.note: the child goes inside the intensifier

parts.note: so means very
a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A baby rides in an ancient sledge in winter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ski-Doo is a snowmobile, a motor sledge used on snow.

clue.text: Circular reef, a ring

parts.note: a bell's toll is its ring

explanation.surface: A ring-shaped reef is simply described as a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: An atoll is a coral reef enclosing a lagoon in a rough loop.

clue.text: Bird expected soon to melt heart of fakir

parts.note: nigh means near, imminent
thaw means melt

indicators.note: the central letter of the holy man's title

explanation.surface: A bird is due to warm the heart of an ascetic holy man.
explanation.definitionFit: The nighthawk is an American nightjar, a bird active at dusk.

clue.text: Going back and forth, virtually unlikely to retain passport

indicators.note: the trimmed word keeps the document held inside it
almost all of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a tall story is an unlikely one
a passport is a form of ID

explanation.surface: A traveller shuttling to and fro is almost certainly keeping a passport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlikely' means tall as in a tall story; 'virtually' drops its last letter to give TAL, and 'to retain' holds the document inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidal water flows in and out with the tides, moving to and fro.

clue.text: Bum that's full of holes

definitions.meaning: a bum is a scrounger, one living off others
a porous bath-time object riddled with pores

explanation.definitionFit: A sponge is a freeloader, and also a porous absorbent pad.

clue.text: Abandoned boy admitting love for legion

parts.note: shed means cast off, abandoned

indicators.note: the youngster lets the zero in, holding it inside

parts.note: lad means boy
O, zero, is love in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A deserted lad confesses his love for a military unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Legion as a noun is a vast number; a shedload is informal British for a huge quantity.

clue.text: Grant's about to cut fruit

indicators.note: the short word cuts into the fruit, splitting it

parts.note: a date is a palm fruit
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone called Grant is poised to slice some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant money is to give it as a gift; the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Item of footwear in toilet ruined, by the way

parts.note: St, street, is a way

indicators.note: the word toilet is wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A shoe is spoiled in a toilet, mentioned as an aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges the six letters to ILETTO, which follows the street abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a woman's shoe with a high thin heel.
